items.front: IVC mature (urban) phase dates, and which metal it did NOT know?
items.back: Mature phase c. 2600–1900 BCE (NCERT); a Bronze/Chalcolithic culture — iron was unknown.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Four phases of the Harappan culture in order?
items.back: Pre-Harappan → Early Harappan → Mature Harappan → Late Harappan.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC

items.front: Who announced the IVC to the world (1924), and who first surveyed Harappa's robbed bricks?
items.back: John Marshall announced it in 1924; Alexander Cunningham (first ASI DG) noted it earlier.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Excavators: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro (early 1920s)?
items.back: Daya Ram Sahni — Harappa (1920–21); Rakhaldas Banerjee — Mohenjo-daro (1921–22).
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC

items.front: Four cardinal boundary sites of the IVC (N-E-W-S)?
items.back: North Manda (Chenab), East Alamgirpur, West Sutkagendor, South Daimabad. Mnemonic MASD.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC

items.front: The Great Bath is found at which single site?
items.back: Only at Mohenjo-daro — a watertight tank on the citadel. (Never Harappa — classic trap.)
items.source: NCERT XII; APPSC GK — IVC

items.front: Site→river: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi?
items.back: Harappa–Ravi, Mohenjo-daro–Indus, Kalibangan–Ghaggar, Rakhigarhi–Sarasvati (Haryana).
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC

items.front: Dholavira: location, water feature, UNESCO status?
items.back: Khadir island, Rann of Kutch (Gujarat); cascading stone reservoirs ('jala durga'); UNESCO 2021, India's 40th.
items.source: UNESCO WHC; APPSC GK — IVC

items.front: Lothal and Kalibangan — signature finds?
items.back: Lothal: tidal dockyard, bead factory, sole port, early rice. Kalibangan: ploughed field, fire altars.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC

items.front: Chanhudaro — what makes it distinctive?
items.back: A craft town (beads, shell, seals, weights) with NO citadel; <7 ha vs Mohenjo-daro's ~125 ha.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Harappan seals: material, script direction, decipherment?
items.back: Mostly steatite; pictographic script written right-to-left; ~375–400 signs; still undeciphered.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Harappan weights: material, shape, number system?
items.back: Chert, cubical, unmarked; lower range binary (1–32), higher decimal (multiples of 16). Bricks 4:2:1.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Mesopotamian trade names: Meluhha, Dilmun, Magan?
items.back: Meluhha = Indus region; Dilmun = Bahrain; Magan = Oman (copper source). Barter, maritime.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Dancing Girl vs 'Priest-King' — material and site?
items.back: Dancing Girl: bronze (cire perdue, tribhanga). Priest-King: steatite/stone, trefoil shawl. Both Mohenjo-daro.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII

items.front: Late Harappan phase dates and hallmark of decline?
items.back: c. 1900–1300 BCE; seals, script, standard weights and long-distance trade fade — de-urbanisation with continuity.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Which Harappan site was the first to be excavated in India after Independence?
items.back: Ropar (Rupnagar), Punjab, on the Sutlej — dug by Y. D. Sharma, 1953–55.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: Which archaeologist found Surkotada, Dholavira and Manda?
items.back: J. P. (Jagat Pati) Joshi of the ASI — Surkotada 1964, Dholavira 1967–68, Manda 1976–77.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: Who excavated Chanhudaro, Lothal and Banawali?
items.back: Chanhudaro — N. G. Majumdar (1931); Lothal — S. R. Rao (1954); Banawali — R. S. Bisht (1974).
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: Which Harappan site in Maharashtra gave a bronze chariot hoard?
items.back: Daimabad, on the Pravara (Godavari tributary) — the southernmost site.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: Which Ahar–Banas site of Harappan times gave India's earliest leprosy skeleton?
items.back: Balathal, Udaipur district, Rajasthan — dug by V. N. Misra from 1994.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: Which two coastal Harappan sites were shell-working centres?
items.back: Balakot (Las Bela, Balochistan) and Nageshwar (near Dwarka, Gujarat).
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: What do the names 'Mohenjo-daro' and 'Kalibangan' mean?
items.back: Mohenjo-daro = 'Mound of the Dead'; Kalibangan = 'black bangles'.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: Kot Diji and Amri (Sindh) are known for what?
items.back: Early / pre-Harappan layers — the 'Kot Dijian' and 'Amri' cultures before the cities matured.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC (Other Important sites); site articles cross-checked

items.front: Where is Mehrgarh and why does it matter for the IVC?
items.back: Kacchi plain, Balochistan; a farming village from about 7000 BCE — the pre-Harappan root.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: What did Mehrgarh's early farmers build and grow?
items.back: Square or rectangular mud-brick houses, granaries, bitumen-lined baskets; einkorn wheat and six-row barley.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Where were the stadium and the ten-sign signboard found?
items.back: Dholavira, Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Which site had two rows of six granaries, and which had the Great Granary?
items.back: Six-and-six granaries — Harappa; Great Granary — Mohenjo-daro.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Match burial type to site: symbolic, pot, joint, dog with man?
items.back: Symbolic — Kalibangan; pot — Surkotada; joint — Lothal; dog with man — Ropar.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Where were bones reported as horse found, and is it settled?
items.back: Surkotada, Kutch (reported 1974); debated — some experts say wild ass.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Decline theories: Wheeler, Marshall, Raikes and Dales, Lambrick?
items.back: Wheeler — Aryan invasion; Marshall — floods; Raikes and Dales — tectonic floods; Lambrick — Indus course change.
items.source: APPSC GK — IVC; NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Why is the IVC called the 'earliest urban' culture of its region?
items.back: It is the earliest known urban (city-based) culture of the north-western Indian subcontinent.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: How is the IVC dated, and what helped it grow?
items.back: By radiocarbon dating; fertile soil, a favourable climate and distinct landscapes aided its growth.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Besides 'Harappan', what other name does the IVC have?
items.back: The Indus–Sarasvati Civilization (many sites lie in the Ghaggar–Hakra/Sarasvati basin).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Which later discoveries showed the same Harappan characteristics?
items.back: Kalibangan, Lothal and Rakhigarhi.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: On what model did the Indus settlements practise farming, per the source text?
items.back: Irrigated agriculture on the Mesopotamian model.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Early Harappan phase dates?
items.back: c. 3300–2600 BCE (Early Harappan), before the Mature phase of 2600–1900 BCE.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Old NCERT / R. S. Sharma date for the mature IVC?
items.back: c. 2500–1750 BCE (current NCERT: 2600–1900 BCE).
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Which metals did the Harappans know?
items.back: Copper, bronze, gold, silver, tin and lead — but not iron.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: What do the seals' moisture-loving plants and animals tell us about climate?
items.back: The ancient climate was fairly moderate, though the region is arid today.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What made the Indus plains fertile?
items.back: Annual floods left rich alluvial soil on the plains.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: When was the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) set up?
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Which regions did the IVC spread into beyond the Indus zone?
items.back: Lowlands of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, highlands and coast of Balochistan, and a coastal strip of Gujarat.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Older alternative for the southern boundary site?
items.back: Malwan (or Bhagatrav) in Gujarat; the modern key is Daimabad.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Which Indian state has the most Harappan sites, and how many sites are known?
items.back: Gujarat has the most; about 1,500 sites are known in all.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Harappa — role as a town and two other finds?
items.back: A gateway city where routes met; bullock carts and sandstone statues of human anatomy.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What stone figure does the source text list among Harappa's finds?
items.back: A stone dancing Nataraja.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Harappa's red sandstone find?
items.back: A red sandstone male torso.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Cemetery R-37 at Harappa shows which burial?
items.back: Coffin burial (body in a wooden coffin).
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: What lay near Harappa's granaries?
items.back: Workers' quarters.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Mohenjo-daro — two public buildings besides the Great Bath and granary?
items.back: A collegiate building and an assembly hall.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Which seal and which fabric are listed among Mohenjo-daro's finds?
items.back: The unicorn seal and woven cotton.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Dates given for Mohenjo-daro in the source text?
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Largest Harappan site in Pakistan?
items.back: Mohenjo-daro (older keys call it the largest overall; today Rakhigarhi is the largest).
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: What did the so-called 'palace' at Mohenjo-daro yield?
items.back: No rich finds — so no proof of a royal palace.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Pashupati figure — faces, horns, posture?
items.back: Three faces, two horns, seated in a yogic posture on a low throne.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Which animals appear below the Pashupati throne?
items.back: Two deer.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Is the Pashupati = Shiva identification settled?
items.back: No — NCERT says it is not straightforward (Rudra is not called Pashupati or shown as a yogi).
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Who excavated Rakhigarhi?
items.back: Amarendra Nath of the ASI (1997–2000).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Rakhigarhi — granary and civic features?
items.back: A mud-brick granary with a rammed-earth floor; burnt-brick houses and effective drainage.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What scientific study made Rakhigarhi news in 2019?
items.back: An ancient-DNA study of a skeleton from its cemetery.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Dholavira — pottery and burials?
items.back: Redware and black-on-red ware; it also had burial grounds.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What does UNESCO call Dholavira?
items.back: The southern centre of the Harappan Civilization.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Dates given for Dholavira in the source text?
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Lothal's town layout and pottery (source text)?
items.back: Upper and lower towns; pottery of black and red clay; coffins in its graveyards.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Lothal lies on which river?
items.back: The Bhogava, near the Sabarmati.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Dates given for Lothal in the source text?
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Where were accurate weights and measures of various shapes found?
items.back: At the Lothal dock.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What national complex is being built at Lothal?
items.back: The National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC), Gujarat.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Who excavated Kalibangan in 1960–69?
items.back: B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Two more Kalibangan finds in the source text?
items.back: Priest quarters and a bronze bull.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Kalibangan — what natural event left traces, and its source-text date?
items.back: An earthquake; dated 3500–2500 BC in the source text.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Banawali — cotton and crop evidence?
items.back: Cotton cultivation (fortified town, terracotta figurines) and good-quality barley.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Rangpur — excavator and crop?
items.back: M. S. Vats (1931); rice (rice husk).
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Bhagatrav — location and role?
items.back: Kim estuary, Gujarat; a small port with bead and shell work (S. R. Rao, 1953).
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Who found Desalpur (Kutch)?
items.back: P. P. Pandya (1963) — a fortified township.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Rojdi — excavator and character?
items.back: Gregory Possehl (1982); an agricultural settlement on the Bhadar, Gujarat.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Bagasra — what industry?
items.back: A shell industry on the Gulf of Kutch (V. H. Sonawane, 1996).
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Sutkagendor — role?
items.back: A fortified trade post near the Arabian Sea linking Harappa and Mesopotamia.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Which two unusual objects came from Chanhudaro?
items.back: An inkpot and lipstick.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: What animal tracks are on a Chanhudaro brick?
items.back: Paw-prints of a dog chasing a cat.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Sothi, Shikarpur and Allahdino — one fact each?
items.back: Sothi — Early Harappan pottery; Shikarpur — shell bangles; Allahdino — small unfortified village near Karachi.
items.examPoint: Other sites — state, river, excavator & finding (consolidated table)
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Who excavated Mehrgarh?
items.back: Jean-François Jarrige (1974).
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: How did the grid roads reach houses?
items.back: They divided into smaller roads joined to the lanes of individual houses.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Three kinds of Harappan buildings?
items.back: Dwelling houses, public buildings and public baths.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What did the citadel and the lower town contain?
items.back: Citadel: granaries, administrative buildings, courtyards, pillared halls. Lower town: one-room workers' quarters and public baths.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What does the uniform layout over a vast area imply?
items.back: Centralised civic planning (a standardising authority).
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Did Harappan houses have windows on the main street?
items.back: No — no windows faced the main street; houses opened onto side lanes.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Great Bath size?
items.back: About 12 m × 7 m and 2.4 m deep.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Harappan crops besides wheat and barley?
items.back: Lentil, chickpea and sesame; millets in Gujarat; rice was rare.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Harappan fruits and non-veg food?
items.back: Pomegranates and bananas; meat and fish.
items.examPoint: Daily life, pottery & art details (food, dress, toys, Red-and-Black ware, terracotta)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Domesticated animals of the Harappans?
items.back: Cattle, sheep, goat, buffalo and pig.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Where were terracotta plough models found, and what do bull seals imply?
items.back: Cholistan and Banawali; oxen were used for ploughing.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Four Harappan occupations?
items.back: Weaving, bead-making, metalwork and trade.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Materials of Harappan beads (source text)?
items.back: Clay, stone, paste, shell and ivory.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Where are specialised bead drills known from, and where did gold jewellery come from?
items.back: Drills: Chanhudaro, Lothal, Dholavira. Gold jewellery: mainly from hoards.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Harappan clothing material and dress?
items.back: Wool and cotton; women wore a short skirt, men a long cloth wrapped around.
items.examPoint: Daily life, pottery & art details (food, dress, toys, Red-and-Black ware, terracotta)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Harappan ornaments and charms?
items.back: Women: bracelets and necklaces of shell, gold and silver. Men: amulets for protection.
items.examPoint: Daily life, pottery & art details (food, dress, toys, Red-and-Black ware, terracotta)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Harappan amusements?
items.back: Clay carts, dolls, rattles and marbles; animal puppets; bird-shaped whistles; gambling by old people.
items.examPoint: Daily life, pottery & art details (food, dress, toys, Red-and-Black ware, terracotta)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What is the 'Priest-King' label based on?
items.back: An analogy with Mesopotamia — it is not proven.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Three models of Harappan authority debated by scholars?
items.back: A single state, several rulers/cities, or an egalitarian society with no single ruler; no royal tombs found.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Which worship forms are attributed besides Mother Goddess and Pashupati?
items.back: Lingam and yoni (phallic) worship, and the sacred humped bull.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: What do grave goods in Harappan burials suggest?
items.back: A belief in an afterlife.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Seal materials other than steatite, and seal shapes?
items.back: Copper, gold, faience, ivory, terracotta; square, triangular, rectangular and circular.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Harappan script — sign count and longest inscription?
items.back: About 375–400 signs; the longest inscription has about 26 signs.
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: Uses of Harappan seals, and one symbol on them?
items.back: Trade, identification marks and educational purposes; the swastika.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Two kinds of Harappan pottery, and how it was made?
items.back: Plain and painted; wheel-made.
items.examPoint: Daily life, pottery & art details (food, dress, toys, Red-and-Black ware, terracotta)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Red-and-Black painted pottery — colours, themes, uses?
items.back: Red background with black designs; trees, birds, animals, geometric patterns; household, decorative, liquor-pouring use.
items.examPoint: Daily life, pottery & art details (food, dress, toys, Red-and-Black ware, terracotta)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What was terracotta used for?
items.back: Fire-baked clay for toys, animal figures, miniature carts and wheels.
items.examPoint: Daily life, pottery & art details (food, dress, toys, Red-and-Black ware, terracotta)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Describe the bearded priest figure.
items.back: A shawl with trefoil patterns; elongated, half-closed eyes as in meditation.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Where are the Dancing Girl and the Priest-King kept today?
items.back: Dancing Girl — National Museum, New Delhi; Priest-King — National Museum of Pakistan, Karachi.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: When does the source text date the Harappan fall, and with what event?
items.back: Around 1500 BCE — the period of the Aryans' arrival.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Four natural decline theories in the source text?
items.back: Floods, eastward-shifting monsoons, drought leading to famine, and a pandemic disease.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: What happened by 1800 BCE per the source text?
items.back: A cooler, drier climate and a tectonic event may have disrupted rivers; people may have migrated toward the Ganga basin.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Is any decline theory proven?
items.back: No — there is no conclusive evidence for any single cause.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: IVC (source text)

items.front: Decline theories of Aurel Stein and Walter Fairservis?
items.back: Stein (and A. N. Ghosh) — a drier climate; Fairservis — ecological imbalance.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Who wrote 'The Mythical Massacre at Mohenjo-daro'?
items.back: George Dales (1964), rejecting Wheeler's massacre idea.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: What happened to Cholistan's Mature Harappan sites by c. 1800 BCE?
items.back: Most were abandoned.
items.examPoint: Late Harappan regional cultures & character (Cemetery H, Jhukar, Rangpur, Bhagwanpura; Chalcolithic villages — APPSC 2024)
items.source: NCERT XII 'Bricks, Beads and Bones'

items.front: How does Daimabad matter for the south / Deccan?
items.back: It shows the Harappan reach into the Deccan; no Harappan site lies in Andhra Pradesh.
items.source: Standard reference (R. S. Sharma / exam-standard brief)

items.front: Which are the world's first three civilizations?
